title: Local magnetic order in vacancy-disrupted spin ice Ho2TiO5
authors: Raju Baral, Haidong Zhou, Qiang Zhang, Benjamin A. Frandsen, Stuart Calder
abstract: We investigate how local magnetic correlations evolve when the classical pyrochlore spin-ice Ho2Ti2O7 is transformed into the partially disordered stuffed compound Ho2TiO5. Neutron scattering measurements were analyzed using real-space magnetic pair distribution function, reciprocal-space reverse Monte Carlo, and half-polarized neutron powder diffraction methods to connect the average crystal structure with local magnetic correlations. Both compounds retain long-range $Fd-3m symmetry, but in Ho2TiO5 this average structure distorts locally through Ho-O, Ti-O and O-O bond-length disorder associated with partial Ho/Ti occupancy. Despite this disorder, half-polarized neutron powder diffraction shows that the Ho moments retain local <111> rangle Ising anisotropy and form spin-in/spin-out configurations on the tetrahedral network. In Ho2Ti2O7, real- and reciprocal-space analyses reveal a nearly ideal two-in/two-out spin-ice state at 0.3K, with 95% of tetrahedra satisfying the ice rule, followed by progressive thermal disordering on warming. In Ho2TiO5, most tetrahedra are magnetically incomplete because some tetrahedral vertices are occupied by nonmagnetic Ti rather than Ho; nevertheless, the dominant incomplete configurations are 2-in/1-out and 1-in/2-out, which are locally compatible with the ice rule if the missing Ho spin is restored. The single-ion <111> Ising anisotropy is therefore retained throughout, while the collective ice ordering is strongly disrupted: Ho2TiO5 is a vacancy-disrupted spin ice in which a local ice-rule tendency persists on a topologically incomplete magnetic network.
summary: This work uses neutron scattering to compare the ideal spin-ice material Ho2Ti2O7 with its disordered analog, Ho2TiO5. The key finding is that structural disorder does not eliminate the local magnetic tendency; instead, it creates a 'vacancy-disrupted' state where ice-rule physics persists on an incomplete lattice. This demonstrates the robustness of local constraints against global structural imperfections.
main_problem: The study investigates how local magnetic correlations persist when the ideal spin-ice material Ho2Ti2O7 is structurally disrupted by partial cation occupancy to form Ho2TiO5.
main_result: Ho2TiO5 retains a local Ising anisotropy and exhibits a 'vacancy-disrupted spin ice' state, where the tendency toward ice-rule configurations persists on a topologically incomplete magnetic network.
method: The research combines neutron scattering measurements (total and half-polarized) with advanced analysis techniques like real-space mPDF and RMC modeling to probe local magnetic order.
model_or_system: The system involves pyrochlore titanates, comparing the canonical spin-ice material Ho2Ti2O7 against the disordered stuffed compound Ho2TiO5. The physics is governed by strong single-ion Ising anisotropy on a tetrahedral lattice.
key_observables: Local magnetic correlations (mPDF), degree of adherence to the ice rule (e.g., 2-in/2-out configurations), and local site susceptibility tensors ($\chi_{\parallel}/\chi_{\perp}$).
important_parameters: Temperature regimes ($0.3 	ext{ K}$ up to $50 	ext{ K}$), occupancy ratios ($2/3$ for disorder).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the local magnetic correlations can be extracted and modeled despite the average crystal structure retaining high symmetry ($	ext{Fd} ar{3}	ext{m}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural models comparing ideal vs. stuffed compounds, and show quantitative data on spin configurations (e.g., fraction of tetrahedra satisfying ice rules) as a function of temperature.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the methods using PDF analysis for local structure determination, followed by polarized neutron diffraction to confirm single-ion anisotropy, and finally applying RMC/mPDF analyses to quantify the deviation from ideal spin-ice behavior in the disordered compound.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the study of disorder effects (vacancy disruption) on emergent quantum ground states like spin ice is highly relevant to understanding frustrated magnetic systems that can be modeled using concepts applicable to correlated electron models or lattice gauge theories.
